abate: A + battre: the wind is beaten down. The storm abated.
Abate = diminish: pain abates after the pill.
acumen: Acus (needle): sharp thinking. Business acumen: spotting a good deal.
Acumen: a mind with a sharp point, like acute.
adulterate: Ad + alter: make other. Adulterated milk is watered down.
Adulterate: cheap filler hidden in the product; not pure.
alleviate: Levis (light): lighten the pain. Aspirin alleviates a headache.
Alleviate: take weight off, like lifting a bag.
approbation: Approve: nod of approval. Seek the boss’s approbation.
Approbation = a thumbs-up; the opposite of opprobrium.
articulate: Articulus: little joint. An articulate speaker joins ideas clearly.
Articulate as a verb: to say it clearly (“articulate your goals”).
aver: Verus: true. Aver = say that it’s true: “I aver my innocence.”
Aver, avérer: to declare with certainty.
bombastic: Bombast: cotton padding. A bombastic speech: padded, empty.
Bombastic = bomb + fantastic: loud and inflated, but a dud.
chicanery: Chicane: legal tricks. A lawyer’s chicanery to dodge the point.
Chicanery: a salesman’s sleight of hand.
circumspect: Circum + specere: look around. A circumspect driver checks every direction.
clamor: Clamare: shout. The clamor of the crowd for change.
Clamor for tickets: everyone demanding at once.
compliant: Comply: do as told. A compliant child tidies up when asked.
Compliant = conforming: your documents meet the rules.
connoisseur: Connaître: to know. A wine connoisseur knows the vintage by smell.
Connoisseur: the friend you ask which cheese to buy.
covert: Couvert: covered. A covert mission is hidden.
Covert ≠ overt: covered up vs open.
desiccate: Siccus: dry. Desiccated coconut is dried out.
Desiccate: dry like a raisin in the sun.
deterrent: Terrere (frighten): scares you off. A high fine as a deterrent.
dissent: Dis + sentire: feel apart. A dissenting judge writes a separate opinion.
Dissent: raising your hand to disagree.
divest: Vestire: clothe. Divest = take off clothes: sell off a stake.
Divest from fossil fuels: sell the shares.
efficacy: Efficax: effective. The efficacy of the vaccine: 95 %.
Efficacy = how well it works in a trial.
eloquent: E + loqui: speak out. An eloquent speech moves a crowd.
Eloquent: Martin Luther King on the steps.
epitome: Epitemnein: to cut short. The epitome of elegance: the pure essence.
eulogy: Eu + logos: good words. A eulogy at the funeral.
Eulogy: reading a loving speech for a friend.
explicit: Explicare: unfold. Explicit instructions leave nothing unsaid.
Explicit: spelled out in plain words.
facilitate: Facilis: easy. A good guide facilitates the discussion.
fervid: Fervere: boil. A fervid supporter chants all match.
guile: Guile: wile, ruse. The fox’s guile.
Guile: a charm used to trick.
gullible: Gull: a swallowable fool; a gull swallows anything. A gullible tourist believes the scam.
Gullible: believes the email from the “prince”.
implicit: Implicare: fold in. Implicit trust: no need to say it.
inconsequential: No consequences. An inconsequential remark: nobody remembers.
Inconsequential: a detail that changes nothing.
indeterminate: Not determined. An indeterminate sentence: no fixed end.
Indeterminate: we don’t yet know the number.
intractable: In + tractable: can’t be pulled along. An intractable conflict won’t be solved.
Intractable pain; intractable problem: nothing works.
lavish: Lavish: rich spending: a lavish party with champagne fountains.
Lavish praise: pouring it on thick.
loquacious: Loqui: speak. A loquacious guest talks all night.
Loquacious: the barber who never stops talking.
nascent: Nasci: be born. A nascent industry: just born.
onerous: Onus: burden. Onerous duties weigh you down. Not « onéreux ».
opprobrium: Ob + probrum (reproach): public shame. The opprobrium of the press.
overt: Ouvert: open. Overt hostility; opposite of covert.
paradox: Para + doxa: against opinion. “Less is more”: a paradox.
Paradox: a true statement that sounds false.
partisan: Parti: taking a side. A partisan crowd cheers only for its team.
plethora: Plethore: fullness. A plethora of choices on the menu.
propriety: Proper: acceptable behaviour. Observe the proprieties at the royal dinner.
Propriety: knowing which fork to use.
tacit: Tacere: be silent. Tacit agreement: no words.
Tacit approval: a nod, no signature.
tangential: Tangent: touches a circle at one point. A tangential remark barely touches the subject.
Tangential: a digression that skims the topic.
tenuous: Tenuis: thin. A tenuous link, thin as thread.
veracity: Verus: true. Doubt the veracity of the report.
verbose: Verbum: word. Verbose email: too many words.
Verbose: the speech that went on for an hour.
volatile: Volare: fly. Volatile liquids evaporate; volatile markets jump.
Volatile mood: from calm to angry in a second.
wary: Ware: aware. Be wary of strangers.
Wary: one eye open, hand on the wallet.
zealous: Zealot: a fanatic for a cause; zealous = very eager.
